findings.obs_text: In Psa 40:17 the Lord takes thought for the poor and needy speaker: the Lord's thought is turned to the poor. In Deu 15:9 the unworthy thought turns the eye grudgingly from the poor brother, and in Joh 13:29 some think Judas was sent to give to the poor. In Ecc 10:20 even in thought one is not to curse the rich. In Isa 55:7 and Eph 3:20 abundantly names God's pardon and power beyond what is thought; in Mic 2:8 the rich robe is stripped from those with no thought of war.
findings.grounds: the Lord takes thought for me

findings.obs_text: In Pro 12:5 the thoughts of the righteous are just, set against the counsels of the wicked; in Phili 4:8 what is just and honorable is what to think on. In Job 35:2 Elihu asks whether Job thinks his claim just. In Mat 15:19 and Mar 7:21 sexual immorality follows evil thoughts out of the heart. In Isa 59:4 no one sues justly where mischief is conceived, in 2Cor 12:6 Paul speaks the truth so none may think more of him, and in Mat 22:17 and Mar 12:14 what is lawful is the question put to Jesus.
findings.grounds: The thoughts of the righteous are just

older.finding: G4202 (porneia, 22 verses, the broadest term) ranges from literal cases (1 Cor 5's incest case, the vice-list entries in Mark 7:21 and Gal 5:19) to a sustained, book-length personification.
older.reason: it states a face or use of the righteous words; the righteous collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Psa 40:17 the Lord who takes thought for the poor is his help and deliverer. In Jer 4:14 Jerusalem is to wash her heart to be saved, while wicked thoughts lodge within: the thoughts stand in the way of saving. In Rut 4:4 Boaz thought to tell the kinsman of the right to redeem, and in Judg 13:5 the son conceived will begin to save Israel.
findings.grounds: wash your heart from evil, that you may be saved

findings.obs_text: In Job 12:5 the thought of one at ease holds contempt for misfortune: contempt is in the thought. In Mat 15:19 slander is among what comes out of the heart with evil thoughts.
